title: Stay Calm. Remain Indoors. Dev Diary #6: Eating My Vegetables
author: AsparagusOk8818
selftext:
*F.C. -4 // W.C. 1999*

*The Treason*  
  
*A vile, wicked blasphemer steals a glimpse of His sign. It was not shown to her; she was not called to it. She spied through bent glass, she tore and pulled, she stripped it naked. She scrutinized; she judged. Her appetite for this pornography would not be satisfied by any feast.*  
  
*She blamed Our Lord Father for the conditions that the Wretched withered beneath. Again and again she cursed Him, spread falsehoods about Him, debased and embarrassed herself until there was nothing left of her that could be forgiven. Then, finally, she Spoke.*  
  
*The Word was small, but alive. And quick. And scared. It ran for shelter and found it among a colony of ants. Though the Word was small, its power was not; the size and strength of its new home expanded to match that power. As did the ants within it.*  
  
*The Roswell Jungle was born.*  
  
…I cannot emphasize enough how gross I feel when I have to “fill out” content for my project.

I’m very happy building characters. Those people live in my head; I want to bring them to life. I love world-building. I love coming up with really specific objects and places that belong in that world.

But then there’s: “We have a shop. The shop needs around 20 items. Each captain needs another 10 to sell. You have cool concepts for four. Fill out the rest.”

Every time I reach one of those parts of the project, I feel like I’m spinning my wheels.

Still, I wanted the shop screen ready by the end of today so I could work on the tactical combat stages tomorrow.

For now, I’m happy enough with how it looks. The briefcases need to be arranged in a 2×2 grid, some wording needs adjusting, and I need to add the encounter track at the top. But this is enough to move forward.

Provisions use an inventory Tetris grid: drag in the items you want, and the game automatically deducts their cost. If they fit, you can afford them, and the shop has enough stock, you can take them with you.

Some rare items are only available in the first shop. If you want something big and dumb, you have to commit to that investment early.

Briefcases are difficulty mutators. The plan is for them to evolve over the course of a run, making things harder while producing Intel. That’s the currency you use between runs to advance the narrative, unlock characters, and reach the personal adversaries of whichever captain you embark with.

Those modifiers stack with the biome’s Terror rating—basically its ascension level. But that’s a discussion for another day.

Getting the provisions screen to *feel* right is going to be an absolute fckn nightmare. The player needs enough information to make decisions, presented clearly, without the whole thing becoming overwhelming.

I’m happy with how it looks. Making it easy to understand is the part I’m dreading. x.x
